chunks: He said: Al-Sharif, the ascetic Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Hamza al-Alawi al-Husayni al-Tabari, may God have mercy on him, reported to me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God's blessings be upon him and his family, said:
"Four things are from the treasures of virtue: concealing one's need, concealing one's charity, concealing one's illness, and concealing one's adversity."

key_terms.الحاجة: Need, necessity (al-hajah) — personal wants or requirements
key_terms.كتمان: Concealment, keeping secret (kitman) — the deliberate act of not revealing something
key_terms.كنوز البر: Treasures of virtue/goodness (kunuz al-birr) — hidden stores of righteous merit

ai.seo_question: What are the four treasures of virtue according to Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) taught that four practices constitute hidden treasures of goodness: keeping silent about personal needs, giving charity privately, not complaining about illness, and bearing adversity without publicizing it. This teaching, transmitted through the Imams from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizes the spiritual value of discretion, self-reliance, and dignified patience in the face of hardship.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 4. He said: Al Sharif, al-Zahid Abu Muhammad al Hasan ibn Hamza al-Alawiy al-Husayni al-Tabari - may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from Abu Ja’far, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Waleed, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Bakr ibn Swaleh, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, who reported from his father and grandfather, peace be upon them, that: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:
"Four (habits) are from the (hidden) treasures of virtue: to keep silent about one’s needs, one’s charity, one’s indisposition and one’s adversity."
